subject: learning/code-startup-fast-forward-main
statement: The shared startup launcher fetches the repository's configured remote branch and fast-forwards the local branch of that name without switching the original checkout or merging into a feature branch; the new worktree still starts from the fetched tip. The pair is the remote and branch in the repository's .pyxis/config.yaml, read through `pyxis shell mainline`; it is origin/main when the configuration sets neither or no pyxis is on PATH. Configuration pyxis refuses, or a name that is not a plain git name, stops the launch before any fetch.
intent: Give wrappers a current mainline source without clobbering in-progress work.
rationale: A plain pull would merge into the current branch. Fetch plus ff-only on local main updates a checked-out main and leaves other branches and uncommitted files put. pyxis init records the branch a repository is actually on, so a fixed origin/main stopped the launch in a repository on another branch or remote. The launcher asks pyxis instead of parsing the configuration, so the shell carries no second copy of the values (config-driven-portability-v1 DINV-4). The remote and branch come from a tracked file and reach git as arguments, so the verb admits plain names only.
fit_criterion: Tests cover fetch failure, fast-forward of checked-out main, and leaving a dirty or feature-branch main unchanged while still creating the worktree from origin/main. They also cover a configured upstream/trunk pair selecting the base while main stays untouched, a refused configuration stopping before any fetch or worktree, and the origin/main default without pyxis on PATH.
learned_from: Operator request, 2026-10-08: the launcher must work in any Pyxis-adopted repository.

provenance.note: Replaces the fixed origin/main base with the repository's configured mainline, and repoints the record to scripts/startup after the launcher moved there.
